avoid_supplements.name: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Cholestyramine binds fat-soluble vitamins in the GI tract, reducing their absorption and potentially causing deficiency with long-term use
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 4-6 hours; consider vitamin supplementation; monitor for deficiency signs

avoid_supplements.name: Digoxin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Cholestyramine may bind digoxin in the gut, reducing its bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Administer digoxin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after cholestyramine; monitor digoxin levels

avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin and anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Reduced vitamin K absorption due to cholestyramine binding may affect anticoagulant efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 4-6 hours; monitor INR closely; may require anticoagulant dose adjustment

avoid_supplements.name: Thyroid hormones (Levothyroxine)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Cholestyramine may bind thyroid hormones and reduce absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Administer levothyroxine at least 4-6 hours before cholestyramine; monitor TSH levels

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential for binding of lipid-based supplements in the GI tract
caution_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; monitor lipid panel response

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May compete for GI absorption though not strongly bound by cholestyramine
caution_supplements.action: Separate administration by 2+ hours to optimize absorption

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: While cholestyramine binds bile acids needed for fat digestion, excessive fat may worsen GI side effects (bloating, constipation, steatorrhea)
avoid_foods.action: Recommend moderate fat intake; counsel patient on dietary modifications to manage GI tolerance

caution_foods.name: Vitamin K-rich foods (spinach, kale, broccoli)
caution_foods.mechanism: Although dietary vitamin K intake is generally adequate, long-term cholestyramine may reduce absorption of dietary vitamin K
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent vitamin K intake; monitor for changes in anticoagulant response if applicable

caution_foods.name: Dietary fiber (excessive amounts)
caution_foods.mechanism: High fiber combined with cholestyramine may increase constipation and GI discomfort
caution_foods.action: Titrate fiber intake gradually; maintain adequate hydration; monitor GI tolerance

monitoring_notes: Cholestyramine is a non-absorbed bile acid sequestrant that primarily interacts by binding substances in the GI tract. Monitor for fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (especially vitamins A, D, K) and ensure adequate separation of dosing (4-6 hours minimum) from other medications. Baseline and periodic monitoring of lipid panel, fat-soluble vitamin levels, and INR (if on anticoagulants) is recommended.
